title: Three-loop renormalization of the N=1, N=2, N=4 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theories
journal: Nucl. Phys. B (2009), DOI 10.1016/j.nuclphysb.2009.03.017; Erratum Nucl. Phys. B1031 (2026) 117660
claim: Three-loop renormalization constants of N=1, N=2, N=4 SYM in dimensional reduction in an arbitrary covariant gauge; beta from gauge vertices (eq. (8)) and from the fermion-fermion-scalar Yukawa vertex (eq. (9), corrected to eq. (12)); after the 2026 correction the gauge and Yukawa couplings renormalize identically for N=1, 2 and 4, so DR is concluded to preserve SUSY to three loops.
theory: N=1, N=2, N=4 SYM obtained by dimensional reduction from D-dimensional N=1 SYM (D = 4, 6, 10)
scheme: dimensional reduction (Siegel) in d = 4 - 2 eps; scalars continued to n_s + 2 eps (e.g. 6 + 2 eps for N=4, from 10d); arbitrary covariant gauge; MS-like subtraction; infrared rearrangement. Original version used the internal-matrix trace identity tr[alpha^r beta^t] = 0 (eq. (10)) valid only for N=4; the corrected version keeps this trace independent, adding eq. (11), which cancels the N=2 three-loop Yukawa discrepancy (coefficient c = -1/4 fixed by N=2).
symmetry_argument: a posteriori SUSY test: equality of beta functions from gauge and Yukawa vertices (gauge-parameter independence also used)

proved: beta_gauge = beta_Yukawa at three loops for N=1, 2, 4 in this DR implementation (after correction)
assumed: the treatment of internal-space (flavour) Clifford traces in d != 4 is consistent; the corrected prescription was fixed partly by requiring the N=2 result (c = -1/4)
checked_partially: agreement at D=4 and D=10 in the original version, mismatch for N=2 (D=6) corrected only in 2026

evidence: eq. (8): three-loop beta from gauge vertices
eq. (9): original Yukawa beta; eq. (10): trace identity valid only for N=4; eq. (11): added term; eq. (12): corrected Yukawa beta

Introduction: Avdeev PLB 117 (1982) 317 had claimed gauge and Yukawa betas differ at three loops in any dimension; this was first shown incorrect for N=1, D=4 by Harlander-Jones-Kant-Mihaila-Steinhauser JHEP 0612:024
Introduction: Avdeev-Chochia-Vladimirov PLB 105 (1981) 272 is quoted as estimating that for N=4 DR works at least up to ten loops for propagator-type diagrams and eight loops for triple vertices
Note added (19 Feb 2026): zero three-loop N=2 Yukawa coefficient obtained in Chakraborty-Moch 2603.02892 (S1a.20)
red_flags: a published three-loop N=2 result was wrong for 17 years (2009-2026) due to an internal-space Clifford-trace identity, i.e. a Levi-Civita/gamma5-type subtlety

the same author's 2010 paper (S1a.11) quotes a five-loop safety estimate from Avdeev 1982 Table 1, whereas this paper quotes ten/eight loops from Avdeev-Chochia-Vladimirov 1981; the primary estimates must be read directly (covered by the DRED-consistency section)
the correction coefficient was partly fixed by demanding the N=2 result rather than derived independently in this paper
cross_checks: Chakraborty-Moch 2603.02892 (S1a.20) explain the discrepancy as Levi-Civita terms in flavour and spinor traces
Harlander et al. hep-ph/0610206 (N=1 four-loop DRED; S1e)
notes: Shows that 'DRED breaks SUSY at three loops' (Avdeev 1982) is no longer the accepted status; the operative issue is the continuation of Levi-Civita/flavour Clifford traces, i.e. the same class of problem as gamma5 in the Standard Model.
